newsitem.title: FRANCE: Few heed Eurotunnel strike call, traffic disrupted.
newsitem.headline: Few heed Eurotunnel strike call, traffic disrupted.

text.p: Few workers heeded a strike call at the Franco-British Eurotunnel Channel link on Wednesday but tourist traffic was disrupted by pickets blocking toll-gates, officials said.
The strike was the first major action by the Eurotunnel unions which had previously only mounted a two-hour stoppage before a fire in the tunnel last November.

Freight traffic and passenger Eurostar trains were not hit by the action, which the unions had called from Wednesday afternoon through the evening. A union source had said it would be widely observed by several categories of workers, including conductors.

"Our leaders have told us to put the French trains in the repair area and leave the way clear for the British trains. We're blocking the toll gates," Franck Heranwal, a member of the Communist CGT union, told a rally of several hundred workers outside its offices.
Earlier this week, a union source said French conductors would board the trains but not operate them, to prevent management calling in British staff who are not strike.

"Half the current personnel are seasonal or temporary staff. If you add to that the fact that the British workers do not want to strike, that those on leave do not have access to the site -- that explains why there are not many of us," Heranwal said.

The unions are demanding better working conditions and accuse management of ignoring grievances over salaries and working hours. They have proposed meeting management representatives, who have suggested July 29 for a first round of talks.
Eurotunnel employs just over 3,000 staff, including 1,600 French workers.
